Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:10:1.hebrew: ואלא קשיא לרבי חייא - דהא איכא למידק מינה דשתים פטור, כדאמרינן: דאי ס"ד כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:10:1.english: And rather, [this poses a] difficulty to Rabbi Chiyya - For behold, one can infer from it that [for] two [dinars he is] exempt, as we said: “For if it enters your mind, etc.”

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:10:2.hebrew: שאני הכא - האי דקאמר שתים פטור, טעמא לאו משום הילך, אלא דקא מסייע ליה שטרא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:10:2.english: Here it is different - The fact that it says [that if he admits to] two he is exempt, the reason is not because of heylakh [“here you are”], but rather because the document supports him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:11:1.english: [If one] claimed against him - His fellow [claimed against him] in court [for] vessels and land.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:11:2.english: He is exempt - For neither his denial nor his admission brings him to [take] an oath.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:11:3.hebrew: חייב - אף על הקרקעות לישבע, כדאמרינן לקמן, שהנכסים שאין להן אחריות זוקקין את הקרקעות לישבע עליהן. משנתחייב לישבע על המטלטלין, זוקקין ומגלגלין עמהם שבועת קרקע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:11:3.english: [He is] obligated - To take an oath even regarding the land, as we say below, that property that does not serve as a guarantee binds the land to [require him to] take an oath regarding it. Once he has become obligated to take an oath regarding the movable property, they bind and extend along with them an oath on the land.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:12:1.hebrew: דומיא דכלים וקרקעות - שכלים שהודה עליהם מונחים לפנינו, וא"ל: הילך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:12:1.english: Similar to vessels and land - That the vessels he admitted to are lying before us, and he says to him: "Here you are."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:14:1.english: They bind - The movable property binds the landed property to take an oath by means of roll-over [gilgul].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:14:2.english: We already learned - In Kiddushin (26a): "Property that does not serve as a guarantee binds property that serves as a guarantee to take an oath concerning them."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:15:1.english: Here is the primary [place] - For this mishna is taught in Tractate Shevuot (38a).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:15:3.hebrew: אגב גררא נסבה - דאיירי התם: נכסים שאין להם אחריות נקנין עם נכסים שיש להן אחריות בכסף, בשטר ובחזקה, ואגב דאיירי דנקנין עמהם, תנא בהדה: זוקקין אותן לישבע עליהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:15:3.english: It cited it incidentally - For [the mishna] there deals with [the rule that] property that does not have a guarantee [i.e., movable property] is acquired along with property that has a guarantee [i.e., landed property] through money, through a deed, and through taking possession [chazakah]; and since it deals with [the fact that] they are acquired along with them, it taught alongside it: They [the movable property] bind them [the landed property] to take an oath concerning them.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:7:1.english: But [had he said] two - For there is no [element of] returning a lost item.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:7:2.hebrew: חייב - מדלא תנא פטור בשתים, ונימא טעמא משום הילך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:7:2.english: [He is] obligated - From the fact that [the Tanna] did not teach [that he is] exempt in [the case of] two [dinars], and let us say that the reason is because of heilekh [“here you are”].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:8:1.hebrew: מודה מקצת הוי - ואינו משיב אבידה, דאיערומי קמערים דלחזקיה בנאמן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:8:1.english: He is [considered] one who admits to part [of the claim] - And he is not [considered] one returning a lost item, for he is employing artifice so that they will presume him to be trustworthy.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:8:2.hebrew: קמ"ל - כיון דבשתים נמי פטור, ליכא למימר איערומי מערים, אלא משיב אבידה הוי:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:8:2.english: It teaches us - Since even for two [dinars] he is exempt, one cannot say that he is employing artifice; rather, he is [considered] one who returns a lost item.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 4b:9:1.english: So too, it is reasonable - That [in a case of] two, [he is] exempt.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:12:1.hebrew: הא כלים וכלים חייב - הוה מצי לשנויי: בחפר בה בורות שיחין ומערות, כדבסמוך:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:12:1.english: Consequently, [if it were] vessels and vessels, he is liable - [The Gemara] could have answered that [the case is where] he dug pits, ditches, and caves in it, as [explained] nearby.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:13:1.hebrew: [הודה במקצת כלים חייב - וא"ת: יהא נאמן במיגו, דאי בעי כפר בכלים והיה מודה במקצת קרקעות? וי"ל: שמא חפץ בקרקעות יותר.] ס"א:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:13:1.english: [If he admitted to some of the vessels, he is obligated - And if you say: Let him be believed via a miggo, for if he wanted, he could have denied the vessels and admitted to part of the land? And one can say: Perhaps he desires the land more.] (In other texts.)

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:6:1.hebrew: אין נשבעין על כפירת שעבוד קרקעות - וא"ת, למ"ד בפרק גט פשוט (ב"ב דף קעה:) שעבודא דאורייתא, מודה מקצת הטענה למה נשבע? הא כופר שעבוד קרקעות! וי"ל, שמחל לו השעבוד, או שאין לו כלל קרקעות, אפי' משעבדי. אבל לרבי יוחנן, דאמר בפ' שבועת הפקדון (שבועות דף לז: ושם ד"ה ואין): כופר בממון שיש עליו עדים חייב קרבן, שיש עליו שטר פטור משום דכופר שעבוד קרקעות — דבעדים לא חשיב כופר שעבוד קרקעות, אע"ג דסבר ר' יוחנן שעבודא דאורייתא, היינו משום כיון שהפקיעו חכמים השעבוד במלוה ע"פ משום פסידא דלקוחות, חשיב כאילו מחל לו השעבוד. ומיירי דאית ליה משעבדי ולית ליה בני חרי; דאי אית ליה בני חרי, אפי' יש עליו עדים פטור, ואי לית ליה אפי' משועבדים, אפילו יש עליו שטר חייב:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:6:1.english: One does not take an oath concerning a denial of a lien on landed property - And if you say: According to the one who holds in the chapter [entitled] "Get Pashut" (Bava Batra 175b) that a lien is of Biblical origin, why does one who admits to part of a claim take an oath? Behold, he is denying a lien on landed property! And it can be answered that [the creditor] waived the lien for him, or that he [the debtor] has no land at all, not even encumbered [land]. However, according to Rabbi Yochanan, who said in the chapter [entitled] "Shevuat HaPikadon" (Shevuot 37b, and Tosafot there s.v. ve'ein): [One who] denies monetary liability where there are witnesses against him is liable to bring an offering; [if] there is a document against him he is exempt, because he is denying a lien on landed property — for with witnesses it is not considered denying a lien on landed property, even though Rabbi Yochanan holds that a lien is of Biblical origin, because since the Sages extinguished the lien in an oral loan due to the loss to purchasers, it is considered as if he waived the lien for him. And [this] deals with [a case where] he has encumbered [land] and has no free [unencumbered land]; for if he had free [land], even [if] there are witnesses against him he would be exempt, and if he did not have even encumbered [land], even [if] there is a document against him he would be liable.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:6:2.hebrew: אין נשבעין על כפירת כו' - לספרים דגרסי בברייתא ר"ע, אין להקשות: הא ר"ע דריש ריבויי ומיעוטי פ"ק דשבועות (דף ד: ושם ד"ה רבי) ובפרק ג' מינים (נזיר לה. ושם), ומאן דדריש ריבויי ומיעוטי אינו ממעט קרקעות כ"א שטרות, כדמוכח בפרק הגוזל בתרא (ב"ק דף קיז:); והיכי קאמר הכא אין נשבעין על כפירת שעבוד קרקעות? וי"ל שיש לו שום מיעוט למעט קרקעות. וכן צ"ל לקמן בפ' השואל (בבא מציעא דף ק: ושם ד"ה ר"מ) אליבא דר"מ, דאית ליה נשבעין אעבדים ולא אקרקעות, ואע"ג דעבדים הוקשו לקרקעות לכ"ע, דמהאי טעמא עבד נקנה בכסף בפ"ק דקדושין (דף כב:); אלא דר"מ דריש ריבויי ומיעוטי להוציא שטרות, ויש לו שום מיעוט למעט קרקעות, ובאותו מיעוט אין למעט עבדים אע"ג דהוקשו לקרקעות, כדמוכח במרובה (ב"ק סג. ושם ד"ה וחד), דמאן דדריש בריבה ומיעט וריבה צריך שני מיעוטי לקרקעות ועבדים. ואע"ג דרשב"א היה תלמידו של ר"ע, אין לחוש מה שחולק עמו והוזכר קודם, דכעין זה מצינו לקמן (בבא מציעא דף ז.) גבי שנים אדוקים בשטר, דפליג רבי עם רשב"ג אביו. ויש ספרים דגרסי הכא ר' יעקב:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 4b:6:2.english: One does not take an oath regarding the denial of, etc. - According to the texts that read in the baraita "Rabbi Akiva", one should not object: Doesn't Rabbi Akiva expound amplifications and limitations in the first chapter of Shevuot (4b, and there s.v. Rabbi) and in the chapter [entitled] Gimmel Minim (Nazir 35a, and there)? And whoever expounds amplifications and limitations does not exclude land, but only documents, as is proven in chapter HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 117b); so how can it say here: "One does not take an oath regarding the denial of a lien on land"? And it can be answered that he has some exclusion to exclude land. And so one must say below in chapter HaSho'el (Bava Metzia 100b, and there s.v. Rabbi Meir) according to Rabbi Meir, who holds that one takes an oath regarding slaves, but not regarding land; and even though slaves are equated to land according to all—as for this reason a slave is acquired with money in the first chapter of Kiddushin (22b)—rather, Rabbi Meir expounds amplifications and limitations to exclude documents, and he has some exclusion to exclude land, and with that exclusion slaves are not to be excluded, even though they were equated to land, as is proven in [chapter] Merubah (Bava Kamma 63a, and there s.v. Vekhad), that one who expounds with "amplified, limited, and amplified" requires two exclusions for land and slaves. And even though Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar was the disciple of Rabbi Akiva, there is no concern regarding the fact that he disagrees with him and was mentioned before [him], for similarly to this we find below (Bava Metzia 7a) regarding "two who are holding onto a promissory note," where Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] disagrees with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, his father. And there are texts that read here "Rabbi Ya'akov".
